newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Rate fear spooks bourses, boosts dollar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rate fear spooks bourses, boosts dollar.

text.p: Leading European shares and Wall Street slid lower on Friday after U.S. jobs data signalled credit may have to be tightened but the dollar took heart and hit a 29-month peak against the mark.

Bourses and currency trading had been marking time ahead of Washington's announcement that 262,000 jobs were created outside the farm sector in December. Wall Street economists had on average forecast only 192,000 jobs would be created.
The closely-watched figures followed a string of data pointing to a strengthening U.S. economy, making an early hike in interest rates by the U.S. Federal Reserve more likely.

Major European bourses, with the exception of Frankfurt, closed down though off their lows, which were hit after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, spooked by the inflation spectre, tumbled by one percent within minutes of opening.
By the time European share trading ended, Wall Street had rallied but was still about half a percent down.

Higher U.S. rate speculation boosted the dollar, which had moved in a narrow range against the mark and the yen for most of the day. It touched a 29-month peak of 1.5858 against the mark late on Friday shortly before European trading wound down.

"The payrolls data has added fuel to the idea the U.S. economy is overheating and the Fed will be forced to tighten," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London. "We don't think the Fed will raise rates in February but a rate hike is not ruled in March."
The dollar was also firmer against the yen, which has suffered to some extent from the massive and continuing selloff in Tokyo stocks.

In other currency developments, the mark weakened sharply against many other European currencies, plunging to its lowest level against the Norwegian crown for more than four years and eroding key levels against the Spanish peseta.

The backdrop of weak German economic data released on Thursday helped to push the mark lower, while the apparent halting of intervention by the central banks of Norway and Spain sped up the decline, analysts said.

Shortly after Wall Street opened, London, Europe biggest bourse, was down 50 points or 1.2 percent. It later recovered somewhat and the FTSE 100 index ended 30.4 points or 0.74 percent lower at 4,056.6, its lowest close for three weeks.
"The nonfarm payrolls were a bit of a shock, there is no doubt about it," said one senior sales trader,

He added that fears of a rise in British interest rates, coupled with a string of downgrades on British company earnings because of recent sterling strength, made for a gloomy outlook for the London market.

A mixed distributive trades survey from the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) on Friday added to London's gloom, with the CBI reporting that clothing, footwear, drugstores and durable goods retailers had a poor December.

German shares fell sharply in line with the debt market after the U.S. jobs data and the IBIS DAX index of electronic trading closed 0.7 percent down, having recovered from lows of 1.2 percent. Earlier, before Wall Street opened, the DAX index of floor trading in Frankfurt had closed at a record high.
It was a similar story in Paris were French shares doubled their losses after the U.S. figures and then recovered slightly to allow the CAC-40 blue chip index to close down 0.9 percent.

One centre which went against the trend was Moscow. There stocks soared to record levels on heavy volume as foreign investors poured money into Russia, dismissing fears about President Boris Yeltsin's health.
The Russian Trading System 24-share index rose seven percent to a record 247.69 on record trading volume for the whole market of $58.23 million.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was trading at 115.85 yen and 1.5855 marks compared with 116.20 yen and 1.5775 marks late in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares closed down 30.4 points at 4,056.6. In Paris, the CAC-40 share index closed down 21.58 at 2,327.5.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 40.76 at 2,933.39 but the IBIS DAX of electronic trading closed down 20.88 points at 2,915.81.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $359.05 compared with its London close of $355.75 on Thursday. Silver ended at $4.77, up six cents.
